newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard-left's view on pensions positive -Treu.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard-left's view on pensions positive -Treu.

text.p: The apparent willingness of the leader of Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation party to discuss working hours and pensionable age "is positive", Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said.

Fausto Bertinotti, whose party brought Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government to the brink of collapse last week, suggested this weekend that the pensionable age could be discussed according to the kind and amount of work one did, saying he was for reducing the number of hours worked.

Refoundation, whose opposition to spending cuts on the welfare state has been rigid, appeared to be showing some flexibility in the party's attitude to future methods of calculating length of service pensions
Treu told reporters attending a business conference, "the trend for a reduction in working hours should be supported."

He said the government's package of job-creating measures to be discussed with unions in talks starting this week contained "planned incentives regarding not only the length of the working day or week but also reductions over longer periods."

However, leader of the main CGIL trade union federation Sergio Cofferati said on Monday he did not see "a link between time worked and pensions," adding that he wanted a wider approach to all aspects of reform of the welfare state.
"The important thing is that the parties making up the government majority come up with a common, joint opinion on the social state," he told reporters while attending a meeting.

Cofferati has said debate between government, industry and unions on general welfare reforms can start this year but talks on pensions cannot start until 1998, a view shared by Refoundation. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
